A.reason: Eigenvalue count equals dimension; S and T have exactly the same eigenvectors (iff, zero vector harmless); conclusion ST = TS.

B.reason: Existential c scopes over the iff, so the hypothesis only says T-eigenvectors are S-eigenvectors; the 'same eigenvectors' condition is lost.

A.reason: a, b are integers (possibly negative) but formalized in N; restricts the domain.

B.reason: Integers formalized as N, and positivity of a, b is also added; excludes negative and zero cases.

A.reason: IsLeast of the set of k satisfying the gcd conditions for all positive n; dropping k>0 is harmless since k=0 fails.

B.reason: Only proves the lower bound 5 <= k; does not show k=5 works (also quantifies over n=0).

A.reason: Sides a, b with area 180 and perimeter 54; diagonal squared a^2+b^2 = 369.

B.reason: Right triangle with legs equal to rectangle sides models the diagonal as hypotenuse; AC^2 = 369 matches.

A.reason: Uses Complex.normSq (squared distance) instead of distance; greatest squared distance is 84, not 2*sqrt 21.

B.reason: Only an upper bound on distances; does not show 2*sqrt 21 is attained, so not the greatest distance.

A.reason: Nonnegative real sequence, product over range n equals 1 implies sum at least n.

B.reason: NNReal encodes nonnegativity; product 1 implies sum at least n.

A.reason: Extra hypothesis exactly excludes negative r (rpow artifact), which the real cube-root reading already rules out; conclusion correct.

B.reason: Real.rpow on negative r is not the real cube root; admits spurious negative r satisfying h0, making the statement false.

A.reason: Arbitrary index family of spaces; sequence converges in the product iff each coordinate converges.

B.reason: Index set restricted to Fin n, so only finite products; the problem concerns arbitrary products.

A.reason: For prime p and every integer a, a^p is congruent to a mod p.

B.reason: Adds coprimality of a and p (and restricts a to N); the claim is for all integers a.

A.reason: Witness p lacks positivity, so p=0 makes m*p <= m+p trivial; the positive-n condition is dropped.

B.reason: Set of positive m having a positive n with mn <= m+n is infinite.

A.reason: Sum mod 100 equals 59 pins the tens digit as 5; standard encoding of the digit question.

B.reason: Head of little-endian digits after dropping the units digit is the tens digit, equal to 5.

A.reason: Primitive root needs order p-1; IsPrimitiveRoot 3 p asserts order p, which is false in ZMod p.

B.reason: 3 elaborates in N, not ZMod p; also order p instead of p-1.

A.reason: Uses intersection instead of union of subspaces; also omits that the field is infinite.

B.reason: Infinite field, finitely many proper subspaces, union is not all of V.

A.reason: Only 0 < x; x = 1 satisfies h1 via log 0 = 0 junk, giving 0 = 27; needs x > 1.

B.reason: x > 1 makes all logarithms defined; conclusion (log2 x)^2 = 27.

A.reason: Arbitrary indexed family of connected sets each meeting connected A0; union is connected.

B.reason: Family indexed by N only (countable), while the problem allows an arbitrary collection.

A.reason: Only asserts Sylow 5- and 7-subgroups exist; normality is not claimed.

B.reason: Group of order 105 has a normal Sylow 5-subgroup and a normal Sylow 7-subgroup.

A.reason: Concludes H is a p-group (false in general) from P being a p-group; not that P is Sylow in H.

B.reason: P Sylow in G and contained in H; P as subgroup of H is a maximal p-subgroup, i.e. Sylow in H.

A.reason: Exists positive n with a^n = 1 in a finite group.

B.reason: No positivity on n; n = 0 trivially gives a^0 = 1.

A.reason: f, f', f'' differentiable on [-1,1], boundary values and f'(0)=0; some interior point has f''' >= 3.

B.reason: Differentiability of f' and f'' only on Icc 1 1 (a singleton), so three-times differentiability is effectively dropped.

A.reason: Omits a > 0, but a <= 0 makes the hypotheses unsatisfiable (sum <= 0 or infinite set); den + num = 929 matches.

B.reason: Positive rational a, finite solution set summing to 420; numerator plus denominator equals 929.

A.reason: Only shows any such n is at least 17; does not show 80325 divides 17!.

B.reason: 17 is the least positive n with 80325 dividing n factorial.

A.reason: Functional equation assumed only at one fixed x, not for all x.

B.reason: Equation for all integers suffices; f(94) determined via integer recurrence; Z domain is harmless here.

A.reason: For positive non-prime n, (n-1)! is 0 mod n exactly when n is not 4; matches the exception.

B.reason: n ranges over N including 0; (0-1)! = 1 is not 0 mod 0, so statement false; problem means positive n.

A.reason: Sums X^p p times (p*X^p) instead of X^i; wrong polynomial.

B.reason: Sum of X^i for i < p over Q is irreducible for prime p.

A.reason: n < 101 with 123456 congruent to n mod 101 forces n = 34.

B.reason: Divisibility of 123456 - n by 101 (no truncation since n < 101) with n < 101 gives n = 34.

A.reason: Literal rendering: bounded E, some f uniformly continuous on E with unbounded image on E.

B.reason: Drops the hypothesis that E is bounded.

A.reason: Adds NoZeroDivisors on R, not in the informal statement.

B.reason: Commutative ring, element of I inter J has nilpotent image in R/IJ.

A.reason: Digit n <= 9 with 11 dividing 2000 + 10n + 7 forces n = 5.

B.reason: Little-endian digits [7,n,0,2] give 20n7; divisible by 11 implies n = 5.

A.reason: Positive a, b with geometric-mean conditions a^2 = 6b and a^2 = 54/b; a = 3*sqrt 2.

B.reason: h2 constrains S1 not S2 (b = 54); Fin 3 wraparound with r != 1 makes h4 unsatisfiable, so hypotheses contradictory.

A.reason: Polynomial factors as (x-a)(x-b), i.e. a and b are its roots; nonzero a, b give (1,-2).

B.reason: Only requires a and b to be roots, not the two roots; a = b = -1/2 also satisfies, so statement false.

A.reason: Preimage of {x} under bijective f equals {f(x+1)}, i.e. f inverse of x equals f(x+1); x = 47/24.

B.reason: Equiv with toFun 5x-12; f(x+1) = f inverse of x implies x = 47/24.

A.reason: Total milk and coffee amounts restricted to positive integers; amounts in ounces are real.

B.reason: Milk and coffee totals restricted to positive integers rather than positive reals.

A.reason: Positive unit values with 9 lags = 20 lugs and 7 ligs = 4 lags give 63 ligs = 80 lugs.

B.reason: No positivity of unit values; a = b = c = 0 allows any x.

B.reason: Only one direction of the 'determine all' answer; no verification that the listed pairs are solutions.

B.reason: Drops the finite-dimensionality hypothesis on V.

B.reason: Continuous p with continuous right inverse f is a quotient map.

A.reason: Only a lower bound 49; does not show the minimum 49 is attained.

B.reason: 49 is the least value of the sum of |(i+1)t - 1| over i < 119.

A.reason: On |z| = 1, partial sums of z^n/n converge iff z != 1.

B.reason: Summand i*z/i is z (not z^i/i); wrong series.
